paragraphs: In the morning, engineers revise routing in EDA software. Around midday, they connect a prototype to an oscilloscope and capture signal glitches. The afternoon brings a pilot-production meeting with the factory and analysis of yield curves and failure points. A late simulation report can trigger timing changes for the next board revision.

In one sentence: build chips and circuit boards. The work includes architecture design, component selection, board layout, prototype testing and debugging, signal and thermal analysis, pilot-production coordination, and hardware specifications.

Management roles emphasize broader decisions, research roles emphasize discovery, and support roles emphasize process execution. The differences lie in deliverables and responsibility boundaries, not a simple reporting hierarchy.

Not entirely. AI absorbs much of the structurable work of Computer hardware engineers, but real-world judgment, final accountability, and interpersonal coordination still rest with people. What cannot be replaced is depth of expertise and judgment (AI exposure 8/10).

Most Computer hardware engineer roles require a bachelor's degree or professional qualification. Education is not the only path; technical ability and demonstrated projects carry greater weight.
